Legation of the United States,
Berne

opener.dateline:
Legation of the United States,
Berne, March 31, 1881.

div.p: The undersigned, chargé d’affaires of the United States of America, has the honor, referring to his notes of March 23 and 29, 1881, to inclose herewith to Mr. Droz, President of the Swiss Confederation, copies or English translations of the documentary evidence of the charge contained in the aforesaid notes against the commune of Böttstein, canton of Argovie, of having assisted to emigrate to the United States two notorious and depraved prostitutes, Fridolina Vögelin and Theresa Hauser, earning their living by their shameless calling.

The undersigned regrets his inability to furnish the High Federal Council with the German text of all these documents, but this omission, so far as it relates to the extracts from the register of proceedings of the commune council of Böttstein, and from that of the church council of Leuggen, can doubtless be obtained at those places, the reference to the volume and page of those registers being in each case given. Should the High Federal Council desire it, the undersigned, will be happy to ask his government to furnish authenticated copies of the originals of the remaining documents.

The inclosed documents furnish an unbroken and unbreakable chain of unimpeachable evidence as to the action of the commune council in forwarding these vagrant and abandoned women to the United States. It is unnecessary for the undersigned to designate the unpardonable action of the commune council by the language which it merits. The views of the Government of the United States concerning this and shipments of a similar nature are sufficiently well known to the High Federal Council. It suffices for the present that the undersigned, in bringing the proof of the guilt of the commune and their unblushing admission of the same to the notice of the High Federal Council, should, on behalf of the Government of the United States of America, forcibly protest against this unfriendly action of a Swiss commune towards the United States, and express the hope that the High Federal Council will at once take measures that these women may be immediately removed from the soil of the United States, which is now polluted by their presence, unless the vigilance of American officials shall have prevented them from landing. Their return by the vessel bringing them would have a salutary effect in deterring other commanes from committing similar offenses, and is greatly to be desired.

The undersigned, while reserving to his government the further discussion of this
question, avails himself of this occasion to renew to his excellency Mr. Droz, President of the Swiss Confederation, and to the High Federal Council, the assurances of his most distinguished consideration.
